title: Air Masses
objective: After this level you can explain why a large body of air takes on the temperature and moisture of the place it sits over.
summary: An air mass is a huge body of air with fairly even temperature and humidity, set by where it formed. Maritime or continental, tropical or polar: its name tells you what it brings.

cards.headline: Some days, the air over your town came from northern Canada.
cards.body: A cold snap isn't made where you stand. Often a huge body of cold, dry air has flowed south, bringing its weather along like luggage. Other days, warm, moist air arrives from the Gulf of Mexico. Meet the air masses.

cards.headline: A giant bubble of sameness
cards.body: An air mass is a huge volume of air with mostly the same temperature and moisture all the way across, and it can stretch thousands of kilometers. It gets its character from where it forms. Air sitting over cold, dry land turns cold and dry; air over a warm ocean turns warm and humid. Then winds carry it, and its weather, somewhere new.

items.label: Put together
points: Continental polar: cold and dry, from northern Canada
Warm and moist: from the Gulf of Mexico

cards.headline: Air masses change on the road
cards.body: An air mass isn't fixed forever. If cold continental polar air moves over warmer ocean, it warms up and picks up moisture evaporating from the sea. And where cold and warm air masses meet, as they often do over the middle latitudes such as the United States, they form weather fronts and can set off big storms. Those fronts are the next level's story.

cards.headline: Air masses: named
learned: An air mass shares one temperature and humidity
It takes on the traits of where it formed

questions.prompt: Match each word in an air mass's name with what it tells you.
questions.explanation: Maritime means formed over ocean and humid, continental means formed over land and drier, tropical means warm, and polar means cold.

questions.prompt: Why is an air mass that formed over northern Canada cold and dry?

options.label: Wind dries it out as it travels south
options.rationale: Its traits come from where it formed.

options.label: It took on the traits of the cold land it sat over
Every air mass starts out cold and dry
options.rationale: Air masses over warm oceans are warm and humid.

options.label: Air over land can't hold any water vapor
options.rationale: It can, just less than air over a warm ocean.

questions.explanation: An air mass takes on the character of its source region; cold, dry land makes cold, dry air.

questions.prompt: Warmer air can hold more water vapor, so the air mass most likely to be the muggiest is _____.

options.label: maritime polar
options.rationale: It's humid, but cold air holds less vapor.

questions.explanation: Maritime tropical air formed over warm ocean: it's warm, so it can hold a lot of vapor, and it picked that vapor up from the sea.
